text.div: This section describes the investigational and noninvestigational trial interventions, including the rationale for dose selection, administration procedures, and concomitant therapy restrictions.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6 TRIAL INTERVENTION AND CONCOMITANT THERAPY

text.div: Exoticillin 500mg film-coated tablets. Nonproprietary name: exoticillin. Pharmaceutical dose form: film-coated tablet. Dosage strength: 500mg.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.1 Description of Investigational Trial Intervention

text.div: The dose of 500mg twice daily was selected based on Phase II data demonstrating optimal efficacy with an acceptable safety profile at this dose level.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.2 Rationale for Investigational Trial Intervention Dose and Regimen

text.div: Exoticillin 500mg tablets will be administered orally twice daily with or without food for the duration of the treatment period.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.3 Investigational Trial Intervention Administration

text.div: Dose reductions to 250mg twice daily are permitted for participants experiencing Grade 2 or higher adverse events attributable to the investigational product.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.4 Investigational Trial Intervention Dose Modification

text.div: In the event of overdose, symptomatic and supportive treatment should be provided. There is no specific antidote for exoticillin.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.5 Management of Investigational Trial Intervention Overdose

text.div: Investigational product will be supplied as blister packs by the sponsor. No preparation is required at site.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.6.1 Preparation of Investigational Trial Intervention

text.div: Investigational product must be stored at room temperature (15-25°C), protected from light and moisture.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.6.2 Storage and Handling of Investigational Trial Intervention

text.div: Site staff must maintain accurate records of all investigational product received, dispensed, and returned or destroyed.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.6.3 Accountability of Investigational Trial Intervention

text.div: Participants will be assigned to treatment using an Interactive Web Response System (IWRS).

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.7.1 Participant Assignment to Investigational Trial Intervention

text.div: Randomisation will be performed centrally using a 1:1 ratio via the IWRS. Randomisation will be stratified by disease severity and geographic region.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.7.2 Randomisation

text.div: This is a double-blind trial. The investigational product and placebo are identical in appearance. The IWRS will maintain the blind.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.7.3 Measures to Maintain Blinding

text.div: Emergency unblinding may be performed by the investigator in the event of a medical emergency. The sponsor must be notified within 24 hours.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.7.4 Emergency Unblinding at the Site

text.div: Adherence will be assessed by tablet count at each visit. Participants with less than 80% adherence will be counselled by site staff.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.8 Investigational Trial Intervention Adherence

text.div: No noninvestigational trial interventions are planned for this trial.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.9 Description of Noninvestigational Trial Intervention

text.div: Background therapy consists of standard-of-care treatment administered to all participants throughout the trial in addition to the investigational product.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.9.1 Background Trial Intervention

text.div: Rescue therapy with short-acting bronchodilators is permitted for participants experiencing acute symptom exacerbation. Use of rescue therapy will be recorded in the eCRF.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.9.2 Rescue Therapy

text.div: No other noninvestigational trial interventions are planned. Any additional medications required for participant safety will be recorded as concomitant medications.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.9.3 Other Noninvestigational Trial Intervention

text.div: Concomitant medications taken within 30 days prior to screening and during the trial must be recorded in the electronic case report form.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.10 Concomitant Therapy

text.div: The following medications are prohibited during the trial: strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, strong CYP3A4 inducers, and other investigational products.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.10.1 Prohibited Concomitant Therapy

text.div: All other concomitant medications are permitted provided they are stable for at least 30 days prior to randomisation.

coding.display: ICH M11 Protocol Section 6.10.2 Permitted Concomitant Therapy
